-73.83861,45.61302.name: AccelLab Inc.
-73.83861,45.61302.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-1.13595,52.62680.name: Leicester Fertility Centre
-1.13595,52.62680.state: Assisted Conception Unit, Womens Hospital, Leicester Royal Infirmary, Leicester, LE1 5WW, United Kingdom
-1.13595,52.62680.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-75.34659,40.61290.name: University Health Network
-75.34659,40.61290.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, June 2024
-75.34659,40.61290.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, June 2024. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-106.57864,35.05593.name: Lovelace Respiratory Research Institute
-106.57864,35.05593.state: 2425 Ridgecrest Dr SE, Albuquerque, NM 87108, United States, United States
-106.57864,35.05593.desc: A BSL3+ laboratory, operational. Run by Lovelace Respiratory Research Institute. It is categorised as a private laboratory, working on human health. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

-1.19700,52.93800.name: Frozen Ark Project
-1.19700,52.93800.desc: A UK-led network banking DNA and viable cells from endangered animals, so that material survives the species. It assumes a future in which stored cells can be turned back into an animal, which is the premise de-extinction companies sell commercially and which this network has been quietly preparing for since 2004 without claiming it can be done.

-76.93500,38.96100.name: USDA APHIS — biotechnology regulatory notices
-76.93500,38.96100.state: Riverdale, Maryland — BRS, 4700 River Rd Unit 98
-76.93500,38.96100.desc: The notices and rule changes through which US oversight of engineered plants has been rewritten, most substantially by the SECURE rule of 2020. That rule let developers themselves determine whether a plant is exempt, with the agency confirming rather than assessing — which moved the initial judgement from the regulator to the company and is why the count of reviewed products fell sharply afterwards.
